episodes.title: Why 60 FPS Can Still Stutter
episodes.description:
A 60 FPS counter can look perfect while one long frame makes the game feel rough. This short animation shows what frame pacing measures, why 16.7 milliseconds matters at 60 FPS and how one 40 millisecond hitch can hide inside a healthy average.

Sources:
https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/smooth-frame-rate-in-unreal-engine
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3ddxgi/dxgi-flip-model

episodes.title: Why PC Games Stutter the First Time
episodes.description:
A new effect appears, the game hitches once and the same scene runs smoothly the next time. This short animation explains pipeline state objects, why a missing graphics pipeline can interrupt a frame and how a cached pipeline changes the second run.

episodes.title: How Games Rebuild Detail From Previous Frames
episodes.description:
A sharp 4K image may begin with fewer newly rendered pixels. This short animation shows how temporal upscalers combine the current frame with motion vectors, depth and history, then reject stale samples that could cause ghosting or shimmer.

Sources:

episodes.title: How Headphones Put Sounds Behind You
episodes.description:
Headphones have only two speakers, yet games can place footsteps behind or above you. This short animation explains positioned sound objects, HRTF filtering and the tiny timing, level and frequency cues your brain interprets as direction.

episodes.title: Why Games Do Not Keep Every Texture in VRAM
episodes.description:
A modern game can contain more texture data than graphics memory can hold. This short animation explains mip levels, camera-driven residency and why a detailed surface may arrive late or disappear when the VRAM budget gets tight.

episodes.title: How Ray Tracing Skips Millions of Triangles
episodes.description:

episodes.title: Why More FPS Does Not Always Mean Faster Input
episodes.description:
